definitions.plain_definition: When things are aligned, structured, and working together in an orderly way.
definitions.used_in_context: Physics has a word for when things are aligned, structured, in phase: coherence.

definitions.plain_definition: When order breaks down into noise and things fall apart.
definitions.used_in_context: And a word for when that alignment breaks down into noise: decoherence.

definitions.plain_definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system.
definitions.used_in_context: The physicist's entropy, the doctor's diagnosis, the ethicist's judgment, and the theologian's discernment are all reading the same dial.

definitions.plain_definition: A mathematical proof that any system complex enough to do basic math cannot prove its own consistency from within itself.
definitions.used_in_context: Gödel, Tarski, Turing, Second Law, Landauer. Same structure. Different instruments. One conclusion.

definitions.plain_definition: A system that is self-contained and does not interact with anything outside itself.
definitions.used_in_context: Either the universe is an exception to five proven theorems, or it isn't a closed system.

definitions.plain_definition: The law that says disorder (entropy) in a closed system always increases over time.
definitions.used_in_context: Entropy always increases. Order always decays. So why hasn't the universe reached heat death?

definitions.plain_definition: The idea that erasing information requires energy, so thinking has a physical cost.
definitions.used_in_context: Information is physical. Erasing one bit costs kT·ln(2) joules. You can't think your way out of decay for free.

definitions.plain_definition: The theoretical end state of the universe where everything is evenly spread out and no work can be done.
definitions.used_in_context: So why hasn't the universe reached heat death?

definitions.plain_definition: The observation that the universe's physical constants are set to extremely precise values that allow life to exist.
definitions.used_in_context: The cosmological constant is tuned to 1 part in 10¹²⁰. That's not a coincidence. That's a signature.

definitions.plain_definition: A number in Einstein's equations that describes the energy density of empty space, which affects how fast the universe expands.
definitions.used_in_context: The cosmological constant is tuned to 1 part in 10¹²⁰.

definitions.plain_definition: A disagreement between two different ways of measuring how fast the universe is expanding.
definitions.used_in_context: The universe expands at two different rates depending on how you measure it. 5σ discrepancy.

definitions.plain_definition: A statistical measure meaning the result is extremely unlikely to be due to chance (about 1 in 3.5 million).
definitions.used_in_context: 5σ discrepancy. One framework resolves it.

definitions.plain_definition: A structural similarity or mapping between two different systems that shows they are essentially the same in form.
definitions.used_in_context: The Triad — Three Lines. No Escape.

definitions.plain_definition: When two different things have the same underlying structure or pattern.
definitions.used_in_context: The Triad — Three Lines. No Escape.

definitions.plain_definition: A Greek word meaning 'word,' 'reason,' or 'principle' that in Christian theology refers to Jesus Christ as the divine order of the universe.
definitions.used_in_context: In the beginning was the Logos, and the Logos was with God, and the Logos was God.

definitions.plain_definition: Something that does not depend on anything else for its existence; it is its own foundation.
definitions.used_in_context: It must be self-grounding — it cannot depend on something else, or we have infinite regress.

definitions.plain_definition: An endless chain of causes where each thing depends on something before it, with no starting point.
definitions.used_in_context: It must be self-grounding — it cannot depend on something else, or we have infinite regress.

definitions.plain_definition: Something that must exist and cannot not exist.
definitions.used_in_context: It must be necessary — it cannot not exist, or the system collapses.
